Luis Krötz

shared/

The shared module is the monorepo's heart: it owns the application shell that every visitor lands on, the workspace orchestrator that keeps seven modules moving together, the build machinery that turns one source tree into twelve browser-tier bundles, and the documentation/test/verification pipelines that hold the whole project honest.

If core/ is the platform (the primitives a UI is made of), shared/ is the operation — how the site boots, builds, verifies, documents itself, and stays clean.

What's inside

PathRole
src/The application shell — <app-root>, the entry point, service-worker registration
build/Vite plugin machinery shared by every module build
scripts/The workspace toolchain — build, test, verify, docs, i18n, media, setup, scaffold
docs/The published documentation tree (what you see at /docs)
tests/Cross-cutting suites — governance scans, test fixtures, coverage sweeps
local-modules/Security-hardened vendored dependency replacements
reports/Shared coverage reports consumed by the docs portal

src/ — the application shell

shared/src is the smallest source tree in the workspace (~10 files) and the most important one: it's the thing that actually mounts. main.ts is the public-site entry point — the file the browser's loader chain ultimately imports — and App.tsx renders <app-root>, the persistent chrome around every routed view.

The boot sequence, in order:

  1. Side-effect imports — service-worker registration, global stylesheet, router, store, the <app-root> custom-element definition, WASM CSS hooks.
  2. Parallel warm-up — the locale's baked data snapshot and the likely route chunk start fetching before mount, so first paint never waits on network.
  3. App.boot — preferences init, data load, lazy dialog/HUD chunk imports, router subscription with progress bar, scroll/resize/theme listeners, intro loader.

Source map

FileWhat it does
src/App.tsx<app-root> — the shell custom element. Owns the persistent chrome: <app-nav>, <preferences-modal>, <lang-dialog>, <cookie-banner>, <stats-hud>, progress bar, and #view-outlet hosting routed views.
src/main.tsPublic-site entry point (modern ESM bundle) — boot order above.
src/registerServiceWorker.tsRegisters the Workbox-generated service worker in production; an available update triggers a hard reload so users never run a stale shell.
src/app/boot.tsShell bootstrap — preferences, data load, lazy dialog/HUD imports, router subscription, listeners, intro loader.
src/app/data.tsLocale data loading — fetches the APP translation node per locale, fans it out, caches the loaded lang.
src/app/input.tsGlobal input listeners — keyboard shortcuts, pointer handlers, preference triggers.
src/app/modal.tsModal-state DOM sync — modal-open on html/body, modifier class mirror, iOS fixed-position scroll lock.
src/app/scroll.tsScroll tracking — #about/#contact section tops, activeSection/onBottom in sync.
src/app/types.tsShared structural types — the APP translation dictionary plus augmented element types.
src/app/view.tsView-outlet reconciliation — same-tag routes delegate to onRouteParamChange; new views lazy-import their chunk then cross-fade.
src/globals.d.tsGlobal type declarations.
src/modules.d.tsModule-specifier type declarations (virtual modules, CSS imports, etc.).

build/ — the Vite plugin machinery

Every module's vite.config.js is a thin shim over these shared plugins. This is where the "one repo, many modules" build model actually lives:

FileWhat it does
build/vite-lib.mjsShared factory for per-module Vite library builds. Each module's vite.config.js calls moduleConfig() so every library emits with identical resolve/external/dev settings.
build/es-targets.mjsThe multi-engine build matrix — every ES tier the site ships (es2016 IIFE → esnext module), its esbuild/terser/lightningcss knobs, and the runtime feature probes the inline browser loader walks newest→oldest.
build/module-public.mjsPublic-asset merge — every module owns its own public/ folder (website SEO files, core workers, earth-playground textures); this plugin merges them into one dist/ tree at build time.
build/i18n-virtual.mjsvirtual:i18n-* modules — the baked translation snapshot. core/utils/data/db.ts imports these virtual specifiers, so every Vite pipeline (root, module, docs) resolves the same SWR seed data.
build/jsx-in-js.mjsJSX transform for .js files — legacy sources that keep a .js extension while returning JSX get esbuild's JSX loader anyway.
build/docs-portal.mjsDocs-portal pipeline — virtual:docs-manifest carries the scanned docs/reports/coverage/src tree; every publishable file is also emitted as a lazy docs-content/<root>/<path>.json payload.

build/docs/ — the docs-portal pipeline

FileWhat it does
build/docs/scan.mjsFilesystem → manifest tree. Scans the publishable roots (docs, reports, src, core, website, cms, earth, docs-exp, local-modules, coverage dirs) into one manifest; files are addressed by stable ids root:path that double as /docs-content/<id>.json fetch paths.
build/docs/render.mjsBuild-time file → HTML renderers: markdown via marked, JSON pretty-print, source files syntax-highlighted, coverage HTML sandboxed.
build/docs/redact.mjsSecret scrubbing for the public source viewer — strips API keys, tokens, and sensitive-looking literals before any source line reaches a published payload.

scripts/ — the workspace toolchain

These scripts are the verbs of the repo. yarn verify, yarn build, yarn test, yarn docs — each resolves into one of these files.

Build pipeline (scripts/build/)

FileWhat it does
build/build.mjsProduction build orchestrator — prebuild runs the complete verify gate first, then this emits all browser targets, packages deploy diagnostics, and generates locale pages.
build/build-targets.mjsMulti-target build runner — vite build once per tier in es-targets.mjs; each tier emits dist/v/<tier>/assets/{js,css,misc}/ (module) or a self-contained IIFE (legacy). Supports LK_ONLY/LK_KEEP_DIST for single-tier iteration.
build/build-locale-pages.mjsPer-locale static index.html files into dist/ — crawlers and no-JS visitors get translated <title>, meta, canonical, og/twitter, per-route hreflang alternates and localized JSON-LD; covers home/legal/about/contact, playground + star-field slugs, and localized portfolio routes.
build/browser-loader.jsRuntime bundle dispatcher inlined into dist/index.html — strict ES5 so it parses on the oldest engines it detects; walks the ES feature ladder newest→oldest and loads the best supported tier.
build/build-wasm.jsWASM build step for the engine.wasm shared by layout/motion math.
build/deploy-info.mjsAssembles dist/deploy-info/ — the "last deploy" bundle the CMS Deploy Info tab renders (Lighthouse, coverage, axe, Snyk/audit, console-scan).
build/generate-sitemap.jsEmits the sitemap index + per-locale sitemap-<loc>.xml, urllist.txt, and localized robots/llms/ai-catalog files — the full route surface: English canonicals, localized slugs, localized portfolio, star-field catalog deep links, and the English-only /docs/** manifest.

Verification (scripts/verify/)

FileWhat it does
verify/verify.mjsThe single quality gate shared by prebuild and the git pre-commit hook: console-scan, typecheck, eslint, stylelint, unit tests, coverage gate, security scan.
verify/console-scan.mjsZero-console policy enforcement — every console.* call is a violation; diagnostics route through core/devlog instead.
verify/coverage-gate.mjsPer-file 100% coverage enforcement — Jest's threshold checks aggregates; this gate requires every authored source file to hit 100% statements/branches/functions/lines.
verify/coverage-gaps.mjsReports uncovered statements/branches/functions for a file, with --source-map decode for the JSX transformer's coordinate shift.
verify/scope-gates.mjsScoped quality gates — hooks/CI run only the modules a change touches (scoped tsc, eslint, stylelint, tests).
verify/security-scan.mjsDependency vulnerability scan — Snyk primary (SNYK_TOKEN), yarn audit fallback.
verify/uncov.mjsUncovered-lines reporter.
verify/test-lighthouse.jsBackward-compatible Lighthouse entry — defers to the post-build audit so Lighthouse never runs before verified artifacts exist.

Tests (scripts/test/)

FileWhat it does
test/run-modules.mjsRuns every module's Jest suite sequentially — shared, core, website, cms, earth-playground, docs — each with its own jest.config.mjs and reports output.
test/merge-coverage.mjsUnions the raw coverage maps from each module run, then re-emits per-module reports filtered to that module's authored source roots. The cross-module union is why each module can claim "100% of its own files."

Docs generation (scripts/docs/)

FileWhat it does
docs/gen-docs.mjsJSDoc → markdown pipeline — extracts @file/@description/@param/@returns from every .ts/.tsx/.js, writes one md page per file grouped by directory into docs/api/ (published under the docs portal).
docs/sassdoc-lite.mjsSecurity-focused replacement for the unmaintained sassdoc package — parses /// Sass comments into the same JSON shape.
docs/sassdoc-vars.mjsInserts /// sassdoc stubs above $var: declarations so the sassdoc pass has comments to parse.

FileWhat it does
i18n/ast-string-extract.jsAST static analysis — detects repeated non-syntactic string literals across the codebase (UI labels, dict keys, API routes) while preserving engine-level syntactic tokens.
i18n/seed-translations.jsPushes new i18n keys to Firebase RTDB (requires .firebase-admin-key.json).
i18n/patch-earth-playground-translations.jsBackfills the earth-playground translation node.
i18n/upload-earth-playground-firebase.jsUploads the earth-playground defaults to Firebase.

media-convert/pipeline.jsThe conversion pipeline — images → mozjpeg q100/q75/q50 + MSSIM-tuned blur-up variants, videos → mp4 scaled tiers, all in the site's exact CDN naming.
media-convert/install.jsGuided toolchain installer — per-platform package-manager detection and install plans surfaced in the CMS UI.
media-convert/zip.jsMinimal dependency-free ZIP writer (DEFLATE via node:zlib) for result bundles.

Workspace orchestration

FileWhat it does
modules.mjsThe module registry — fixed core modules plus dynamic discovery of any experiments/<name>/ with a package.json.
module.mjsLifecycle fan-out — runs install/dev/build/test/preview/test:coverage in one or every module that defines the script.

local-modules/ — security-hardened vendored deps

Some npm dependencies are unmaintained and carry unresolved advisories. Rather than wait upstream (or accept the risk), the repo vendors replacements under shared/local-modules/, wired in via package.json resolutions.

ModuleWhy it's vendored
local-modules/braces/GHSA on braces <=3.0.3 — recursive {{{{…}}}} nesting exhausted the call stack before range/limit checks ran. Patched so parse/expand iterates safely.
local-modules/extract-zip/Unmaintained; two advisories — unvalidated symlink path traversal and an overwrite vulnerability. This drop-in validates every entry against the target dir.
local-modules/sprintf-js/Vendored utility with its own helpers.

docs/ — the published documentation tree

shared/docs/ is the docs: root the portal scans — everything here is what you browse at /docs. README.md inside is the documentation index; architecture/ and guides/ hold the curated prose; api/ is generated by gen-docs.mjs.

See shared/docs/README.md for the full reading map.

tests/ — cross-cutting suites

shared/tests/ hosts the suites that don't belong to any single module: governance scans (the zero-hardcoding/zero-console/token-ownership guards), test fixtures, the coverage sweeps spanning modules, and the shared Jest preset (jest.preset.mjs) + resolver + setup every module config extends.

Commands

yarn setup        # guided environment install (node/yarn/git/hooks/media tools)
yarn dev          # dev server for the full site (all modules mounted)
yarn verify       # the complete quality gate — format, scans, type, lint, tests, coverage, security
yarn build        # production build — verify first, then all browser tiers into dist/
yarn preview      # serve dist/ exactly like production
yarn test         # run every module's Jest suite sequentially + merge coverage
yarn docs         # regenerate docs/api + sassdoc + typedoc

The module-level commands (yarn dev inside core/, website/, etc.) run through scripts/module.mjs — see each module's README for its own workspace.
